ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The circuit diagram shows an ideal op-amp. A 1 V source is connected to the non-inverting (+) input through a 1 kΩ resistor. The op-amp output is fed back to the inverting (−) input through another 1 kΩ resistor. The output node also connects to a 1 kΩ load resistor RL going down to ground, with the load current IL indicated downward through the load. Reasoning: For an ideal op-amp with negative feedback, the input currents are zero and the two input voltages are virtually equal. Since no current enters the + input, there is no voltage drop across the 1 kΩ resistor from the 1 V source, so V+ = 1 V. Therefore V− = 1 V. Since no current enters the − input, there is no drop across the 1 kΩ feedback resistor, so the output voltage is also Vout = 1 V. The load is 1 kΩ from output to ground, so IL = Vout / RL = 1 V / 1 kΩ = 1 mA, flowing downward as drawn.
